rooms.name: Road (west)
notes: You are on the road, looking east: white render, a timber-batten car gate and a batten gate for people.
The pedestrian gate and the main door both sit in the 3rd–4th of the nine west-side padas, counted from the south-west (Sugriva and Pushpadanta), the ones Vastu recommends for a west-facing entrance.

rooms.name: Front garden & gates
notes: The 0.9 m front setback stays unpaved: a planted bed with a frangipani and stepping stones from the gate.

rooms.name: Laundry under the stair
notes: The washing machine and utility sink sit under the high end of the stair, by the main door, with 2.2–2.7 m of headroom.
Clothes go straight up the stair to dry on the roof.

rooms.name: Stair
notes: One straight stair, repeated directly above itself on every floor, along the south wall. It climbs towards the west: the Vastu-preferred direction (east to west), in the south of the plot.
Each storey has 17 risers of about 185 mm (an odd number, as Vastu prefers) and 250 mm treads, 1.0 m wide, with a 1 m rest landing midway. No U or L turns.
You arrive at the front of each floor facing west and turn right (clockwise) into the room. The next flight starts at the back, directly above the one you came up.

The room side has a short solid wall that rises with the stair, with rounded edges and a timber handrail on top; the floor edge of each stairwell has a 1.0 m wall of the same kind. A second handrail runs on the south wall, and a skylight over the stairwell lights all three floors.
The laundry and storage fit underneath the ground flight. Structurally each flight is an RCC waist slab from the floor beam to the rest-landing beam, carried on the south-wall columns.

rooms.name: Entrance foyer
notes: The main door is 1.06 × 2.40 m, rectangular, with the same vertical timber battens as the car gate. It faces west, in the auspicious padas, 2.4 m from the gate.
Inside, a shoe cabinet and bench. The laundry is on your right under the stair; the entry hall runs straight ahead beside the stair to its foot.

rooms.name: Entry hall & stores
notes: A locked 1.2 m entry hall runs beside the stair, lit through the glass screen from the car porch. Under the stair: a cupboard below the rest landing and drawers below the low end. Tall cupboards stand at the far end.
At the end, turn right round onto the first step: the stair climbs back towards the front, westwards, as Vastu prefers.
Utility use at stilt level should be confirmed with the authority, as stilts are meant for parking.

rooms.name: Store
notes: A store opening off the car porch for tools, pump controls and garden things.

rooms.name: Entry porch
notes: A short planted porch under the first-floor loggia, with a black-and-white checkerboard floor, leads from the gate to the main door.

rooms.name: Car porch (stilt)
notes: Your car parks in the north-west, which Vastu prefers for vehicles. The motorcycle is behind it, with room for a second car in tandem.
The underground sump sits under the north-east end, where Vastu wants water storage below ground.

rooms.name: North side setback
notes: Kept open and unpaved. Vastu favours more openness to the north and east, and this strip lets the north windows breathe.

rooms.name: Rear setback
notes: A 0.7 m rear setback for the rainwater recharge pit and the kitchen chimney outlet.

rooms.name: First-floor stair foot
notes: The next flight up starts here at the back, beside the kitchen, directly above the flight below.

rooms.name: Pooja corner
notes: An open mandir corner in the north-east (Ishanya), kept open and light, as Vastu likes.
The walnut mandir unit stands against the east wall with the idols facing west, so you pray facing east. No toilet is near it.

rooms.name: Living room
notes: The living room is now about 3.3 × 2.9 m, about 45% bigger: a 2.0 m three-seater, an armchair and a coffee table face a 50" TV between two north windows (window, TV, window), open to the kitchen.
It grew because the bathroom moved inside bedroom 1, so the bedroom could shift west into space the hall did not need.
The second-floor family lounge is the larger gathering space.

rooms.name: Kitchen
notes: The kitchen is in the south-east (Agni corner), the Vastu-preferred spot. The hob is on the east wall, so the cook faces east.
The sink is on a slim 1.40 × 0.60 m island parallel to the counter, with a 1.06 m aisle. A window over the counter and a ducted chimney take the fumes out.
Storage: overheads and a loft on the east wall, and a tall pull-out pantry and the fridge on the south wall.

rooms.name: Bedroom 1 ensuite
notes: The first-floor bathroom is now inside bedroom 1, in its north-west corner (a Vastu-preferred spot for toilets): WC, basin and a hand shower.
Living-room guests reach it through the bedroom. It is ventilated through an obscure-glass window onto the loggia and a high north window.

rooms.name: Bedroom 1
notes: Bedroom 1 now runs from the loggia to the living-room wall, with its own bathroom in the north-west corner and a sliding door to the loggia.
A 4.5 ft double bed with its head to the east (Vastu-preferred), a 1.64 m wardrobe along the north wall under a clerestory window. About 7 m² of bedroom floor plus the ensuite.
It sits in the west-north of the floor, which Vastu suits for children or guests.

rooms.name: First-floor loggia
notes: A 1.35 m deep loggia behind two arches, reached from bedroom 1 by a steel-framed slider; the landing window looks onto it too. It shades the west glass.

rooms.name: Front hall & landing
notes: The stair arrives here at the front. Turn right: bedroom 1 is straight ahead, and the hall runs along the stair to the living room, kitchen and the next flight at the back.

rooms.name: Family lounge
notes: A family lounge where everyone can spend time together. You arrive into it straight off the stair at the front: turn right and you are in.
The second-floor balcony is enclosed: steel-framed glass fills both arches above a 0.45 m sill and opens for breeze. An L-shaped sofa, a coffee table, a window seat, and no TV.
The west glass gets afternoon sun. Use low-e glass and fit blinds or bamboo chiks inside the arches.

rooms.name: Reading nook
notes: The north corner of the enclosed balcony: an armchair and an indoor planter under the glazed arch.

rooms.name: Master ensuite
notes: A north-west ensuite (Vastu-friendly for toilets): shower, WC and basin, with a high obscure window and an exhaust duct.

rooms.name: Master bedroom
notes: About 9.3 m²: a queen bed with its head to the south, a 1.67 m wardrobe with a loft, a north window, and the ensuite through a pocket door.
Vastu note: the master sits nearer the north-centre, which is weaker than the south-west (the stair takes the south). The bed faces correctly.

rooms.name: Upper hall
notes: The hall runs from the lounge along the stair to the guest room and to the roof flight at the back.

rooms.name: Guest room / study
notes: A guest room or study: a queen bed with its head to the east, a 1.6 m wardrobe and its own ensuite.
It sits in the north-east, which Vastu suits for study.

rooms.name: Guest ensuite
notes: WC, basin and shower, in the south-east, a Vastu compromise noted in the report. Its exhaust duct runs to the roof.

rooms.name: Stair cabin
notes: The stair lands at the front inside a small cabin under a glass skylight. The water tank sits on top, in the south-west.

rooms.name: Roof garden
notes: Turn right out of the cabin onto the garden: raised planters, a lawn under a timber pergola, a bench and a low table.
The water tank sits on the cabin in the south-west, the heavy corner, as Vastu advises. The north-east of the roof is kept light: only solar panels and drying lines.

rooms.name: Drying deck
notes: Drying lines in full sun beside raised solar panels.
